newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest seen wet, colder through Friday.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest seen wet, colder through Friday.

text.p: The corn and soybean harvest will likely come to a halt in parts of the eastern U.S. Corn Belt Thursday and Friday as a band of showers moves across Illinois and into Indiana and Ohio, meteorologists said.
"I'm going with 0.10 to 0.75 inch (rain) for Illinois, Indiana and Ohio for the next 36 hours," said Fred Gesser, chief forecaster for Weather Express.
Temperatures were expected to peak in the 40s F Friday, with 20s and 30s F for morning lows, said Joel Burgio, meteorologist with Weather Services Corp.
"It looks like we'll freeze some of the areas that haven't frozen yet," Burgio said. He put the freeze line from Des Moines, Iowa to Peoria, Ill.
Heavy winds were also seen battering the western Midwest with gusts up to 50 miles per hour possible, Burgio said.

"The big news is an intensifying area of low pressure," Burgio said. "This is going to generate a good deal of wind across that northwest part of the belt with some gusts more than 50 mph tonight and tomorrow."
Some northwest regions could see snow on Friday with the heaviest accumulations in the Dakotas and western Minnesota.
Rains should move out of the Midwest by Saturday but some clouds could linger in the eastern Corn Belt, Gesser said.
"I think the precipitation is going to be done" by Saturday, Gesser said.
Long-range forecasts indicated another rain event moving into the corn belt Monday and Tuesday, Burgio said.
